summary: The SAFEGUARDS Act of 2026 changes how the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) allocates revenue collected from the passenger security fee (commonly known as the 9/11 security fee). Instead of sending a larger portion of these fees to the Department of the Treasury general fund for debt reduction, the bill directs the first $500 million collected each fiscal year starting in 2028 into the Aviation Security Capital Fund, and the next $250 million into a newly established Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund. These funds are designated for airport security equipment, such as baggage screening systems and checkpoint technology.

affected_groups.effect: Receives increased and dedicated funding streams starting in fiscal year 2028 for baggage screening systems and checkpoint technology.
Pay passenger security fees whose revenues are redirected away from the general treasury fund and toward dedicated aviation security infrastructure funds.

key_provisions: Expresses the sense of Congress that passenger security fees should be used exclusively for commercial aviation security and that the diversion of these funds to other purposes should end no later than 2027.

Requires the first $500 million collected each fiscal year (beginning in fiscal year 2028) from passenger security fees to be deposited into the Aviation Security Capital Fund, an increase from the previous requirement of $250 million.

Grants the TSA Administrator authority to use the Aviation Security Capital Fund to make grants or enter into agreements for acquiring and installing in-line baggage screening systems and other airport security improvements.
Establishes a new Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund within the Department of Homeland Security.

Requires the next $250 million collected each fiscal year (beginning in fiscal year 2028) from passenger security fees to be deposited into the new Aviation Security Checkpoint Technology Fund for testing, procuring, deploying, installing, and sustaining checkpoint technology.
missing_information: The total amount of passenger security fees collected annually beyond the specified $750 million is not detailed.
The specific impact on general fund debt reduction resulting from the reduced fee allocations is not quantified.
